answer: Decaying Reputation Multiplier: each new identity starts at a low weight vertex in the trust graph. Its influence grows only after sustained valid activity across a fixed time horizon, so operating many fresh identities yields near-zero aggregate weight. An attacker must fund and run each identity through the full ramp period before it counts, multiplying real cost per usable unit by the ramp length. Honest actors pass through one grove of identities cheaply; mass fabrication pays that ramp cost thousands of times over.
